robot.def: A machine that senses the world, decides something, and then moves or acts on its own.

actuator.def: Any part that makes a robot move or act — like a motor or a buzzer.

sensor.def: A part that lets the robot notice things, like distance, light, or touch.

loop.def: A way to repeat the same steps over and over without writing them twice.

conditional.def: An 'if this, then that' decision in a program.

variable.def: A named box in a program where you store a value to use later.

led.def: A tiny light (Light-Emitting Diode) — the 'hello world' of electronics.

circuit.def: A complete loop that electricity can flow around.

motor.def: An actuator that spins — robots use them to drive wheels.

microcontroller.def: A small, cheap computer chip that runs one program — the robot's brain.

torque.def: Twisting strength — how hard a motor can turn, not how fast.

gear.def: A toothed wheel that trades speed for strength (or the reverse) between motors and wheels.

current.def: How much electricity is flowing — like the amount of water moving through a hose.

voltage.def: The push behind electricity — like water pressure in a hose.

event.def: Something that happens and starts code running — a button press, a timer, a sensor tripping.

resistance.def: How much a material fights the flow of current, measured in ohms (Ω). More resistance, less current for the same push.

ohms-law.def: The rule linking the three: current = voltage ÷ resistance (I = V ÷ R). Know two, you can always work out the third.

gear-ratio.def: How many turns of the driving gear it takes to turn the driven gear once. A 3:1 ratio means three times slower and roughly three times more torque.

power.def: How fast energy is delivered. For a spinning motor it is roughly torque × speed — which is why gears can trade one for the other but never create more of both.

polling.def: Checking a sensor over and over inside a loop to see if anything changed. Simple, but the robot is blind between checks.

interrupt.def: A signal that makes the microcontroller drop what it is doing and handle something immediately. This is what an event block becomes on real hardware.

threshold.def: The value a sensor reading is compared against to make a decision — the 'stop if closer than this' number.

pwm.def: Pulse-width modulation: switching power on and off very fast so a motor or LED behaves as if it were getting a fraction of full power. This is how 'set speed to 2' works on a real robot.
